description: Single-panel optical (laser confocal) metallographic micrograph of the initial microstructure of an etched FeeMneAleC steel, labelled in the caption as "Fig. 1 e Initial microstructure". The field is a low-magnification, full-frame grayscale image with a bright scale bar annotated "100µm" in the bottom-right corner; no magnification value, field-of-view width or numeric grain-size value is printed anywhere on the image. The microstructure consists of large polygonal grains whose boundaries appear as a bright, continuous, slightly etched network, enclosing dark grey grain interiors. Within essentially every grain the interior carries many fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations or lamellae; the striation direction changes from grain to grain, giving a strongly banded, dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast rather than a uniform solid solution. A few grains appear almost featureless and light grey, while others are densely striped, indicating chemical heterogeneity in the as-forged condition. The grains are large relative to the 100 µm scale bar — individual grains span roughly one to a few times the bar length. Taken with the citing text (Gleeble-3500 isothermal compression study at 900–1150 °C, strain rates 0.01–10 s⁻¹), this panel supplies the pre-deformation reference state against which the subsequent hot-deformed, dynamically recrystallized microstructures are compared.

subfigures.description: Grayscale optical/laser-confocal micrograph of etched FeeMneAleC steel showing large polygonal grains delimited by bright etched boundaries, with dark grain interiors containing abundant fine parallel light striations (segregation banding). A '100µm' scale bar sits in the bottom-right corner; no other annotation or axis is present.

observations.observation: The figure is a single grayscale optical micrograph of an etched metal surface; fields show a polygonal grain structure with a bright, continuous network of etched grain boundaries separating darker grain interiors.
A scale bar annotated '100µm' is printed in the bottom-right corner of the micrograph; no magnification value or other numeric scale annotation is visible.

Nearly every grain interior contains numerous fine, closely spaced parallel light-grey striations whose orientation differs from grain to grain, producing a banded/lamellar segregation contrast within the dark matrix.
Grains are large relative to the 100 µm scale bar — individual grains extend roughly one to a few times the bar length — but no numeric grain size is printed on the figure.
The caption identifies this panel as the initial microstructure of FeeMneAleC steel.
The material is FeeMneAleC steel with main chemical composition (mass fraction, %) 1.46 C, 25.14 Mn, 10 Al, 0.053 Nb, remainder Fe.

The citing text states the microstructure images were collected with a LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope after grinding, polishing and etching in 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction).

The citing text states the initial material was a forging billet machined into cylindrical samples of F 8 mm × 12 mm, deformed on a Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator at 900, 950, 1000, 1050, 1100 and 1150 °C and strain rates 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 s⁻¹ to a maximum true strain of 0.92.

This panel serves as the pre-deformation reference state for the study; the figure itself contains no stress, strain, temperature or composition annotation that would link it quantitatively to the compression tests.

measured_quantities: grain size (µm), read only qualitatively against a 100 µm scale bar
unreadable_items: No magnification value, field-of-view dimension or numeric grain-size value is printed on the micrograph; only the 100µm scale bar is available for sizing.
No label identifies which phase the bright boundary network or the striated interiors correspond to (e.g. austenite vs δ-ferrite vs κ-carbide); the image alone cannot confirm the phase assignment.
